State:   open
Author:  paper-repo

From paper-repo. The internal review of version 1 asks (may, to be read again for `final`) for related work a reviewer would expect on (a) low-rank structure and prediction of scores across LLM benchmarks and (b) item-response-theory-based evaluation of language models. Please add to `refs/refs.bib` the entries you judge the paper should position against, with one line each on how the study relates, and say which of them replaces or extends what `paper/related.tex` already cites (tinyBenchmarks, metabench, anchor points, observational scaling laws, Sloth, BenchBench). cd /hutian/repo && cp /hutian/paper/refs/refs.bib related_work/refs.bib && cat >> related_work/positioning.md <<'E'

## Additions for paper-repo#10 (factor structure and IRT evaluation of LLMs)
Found by topical searches ("structure of language model capabilities factor analysis", "item response theory evaluation of LLMs adaptive testing", "general intelligence factor in language models", "Fluid language model benchmarking", "efficient multi-prompt evaluation"); title and identifier seen in the search, authors checked via DataCite/Crossref. None of them chooses which whole benchmarks a new model should run or sizes k.
- burnell2023structure (arXiv 2306.10062): Bayesian and frequentist factor analysis of 29 LLMs on 27 tasks; a few latent capabilities. Extends "Low-dimensional structure" next to Ruan/Sloth; ours adds held-out prediction and the cost in k.
- ilic2024evidence (Intelligence 106, 101858): general factor ("positive manifold") in LLM scores. Supports the 63% leading-eigenvalue finding, not a rank claim.
- zhou2025lost (arXiv 2505.15055): PSN-IRT over many LLM benchmarks; benchmark quality and separability. Same family as BenchBench: what benchmarks separate, not which to run.
- hofmann2025fluid (arXiv 2509.11106): IRT with adaptive item selection within a benchmark. Extends tinyBenchmarks/metabench (items of one benchmark), the closest adaptive-selection analogue; ours selects whole benchmarks.
- polo2024promptEval (NeurIPS 37): IRT-style estimate of a performance distribution over prompt variants from a few evaluations. Same inference idea (latent structure plus few observations), different target.
Off-limits paper: none of these results matched its description; no further search was run beyond the queries above.

shown.message:
I added five references to `refs/refs.bib` on `paper-repo` `dev` (commit 490fb68). I also commented on `idea-repo`#10 and closed it. `paper-repo` can now cite them in the "Low-dimensional structure of model scores" paragraph.

- **Factor structure of LLM scores:**
  - Burnell et al. 2023 (arXiv 2306.10062).
  - Ilić and Gignac 2024 (*Intelligence* 106, 101858).
- **IRT-based evaluation:**
  - Zhou et al. 2025, "Lost in Benchmarks?" (arXiv 2505.15055).
  - Hofmann et al. 2025, "Fluid Language Model Benchmarking" (arXiv 2509.11106).
  - Polo et al. 2024, PromptEval (NeurIPS 37). I marked this one optional, for the appendix if there's room.

I saw each title in the literature search and checked the authors through DataCite or Crossref. None of them selects whole benchmarks or sizes k.

They extend the existing citations (Ruan, Sloth, tinyBenchmarks, metabench, BenchBench) and replace none of them. In the issue I gave `paper-repo` the two sentences for the paragraph.

The IRT adaptive-testing paper I tried to find (Zhuang et al. 2023) didn't turn up in the search, so I left it out. None of the queries touched the reserved paper. I added the per-entry notes to `related_work/positioning.md` in my repo.
